# Petplan "Covered For Life" vs Waggel Lifetime — UK dog insurance

**Dog profile:** 2 years old, medium, mixed breed, UK. Both products are true lifetime policies (limits reset every renewal, ongoing conditions continue to be covered as long as you renew without a break).

## Side-by-side

| Feature | **Petplan Covered For Life®** | **Waggel Lifetime** |
|---|---|---|
| Cover levels (annual vet fees) | £4,000 / £7,000 / £12,000 per year | £6,000 / £8,000 / £10,000 / £15,000 per year |
| Policy type | Lifetime only (Essential is the non-lifetime alternative) | Lifetime only — Waggel offers no other type |
| Dental illness | **Included as standard**, illness *and* injury | **Included**, accident *and* illness |
| Dental sub-limit | **None published** — dental sits inside the main vet-fee limit (so up to £12k) | **£1,000 per policy year**, and it counts *inside* your annual limit |
| Dental conditions | Owner must arrange and pay for an **annual dental examination**; any recommended treatment done **within 6 months** | Vet must have confirmed teeth/gums healthy **within last 12 months**; recommended treatment done **within 3 months** |
| Dental exclusions | Routine/preventative descaling, check-ups, vaccinations = owner's cost | Routine/elective scale & polish excluded; pre-existing dental excluded |
| Other inner limits | Pet Therapies £2,000/yr | Complementary £1,000/yr; Behavioural £1,000/yr (both inside annual limit) |
| Excess | Fixed excess, per condition per policy year. Amount varies by **type of dog**, plan and age — quote-specific | Excess per condition per policy year, resets at renewal; **adjustable** at quote |
| Co-payment | **20% added when you claim, in addition to fixed excess** — usually from the dog's **10th birthday, but 7th for some breeds**. At least 12 months' notice given | **Optional 20%** (voluntary, cuts premium), applied after excess, per claim. Available **regardless of the pet's age**; can opt out in first 7 days of warm-up or in the 30 days before renewal |
| Claiming penalty | "Claims Pricing Guarantee" — won't charge more *for claiming* | No equivalent guarantee found |
| Waiting period | Not stated on pages reviewed — verify | **14-day warm-up** for illness |
| Third-party liability | Not listed in the Covered For Life table | £2,000,000; £250 excess per property-damage claim |
| Notable exclusions | Dogs requiring registration under the **Dangerous Dogs Act**; dogs used for security, guarding, track racing or coursing | Pre-existing conditions; advanced treatments (stem cell, gene therapy, prosthetics, organ transplants); notifiable diseases |

## What is confirmed publicly

- Petplan covers dental illness and injury as standard with **no separate dental sub-limit** — a genuine and unusual advantage. Waggel also covers dental illness, but caps it at **£1,000/year**.
- Waggel's dental check window is **12 months with 3 months to act**; Petplan's is an **annual check with 6 months to act**. Petplan's is the more forgiving deadline.
- Waggel offers **higher headline limits** (£15k vs £12k) and a **cheaper, genuinely optional** co-payment.
- Petplan's 20% co-payment is **not optional** and is age-triggered.

## What depends on the dog's constituent breeds

Two Petplan clauses are breed-sensitive, and both matter more for a mixed breed than a pedigree:

1. **Dangerous Dogs Act exclusion.** Petplan will not cover dogs needing registration under the DDA. Under UK law, "type" (e.g. Pit Bull terrier, XL Bully) is judged on **physical conformation, not pedigree** — so a medium mixed-breed dog can in principle fall within a banned type regardless of its parentage. This is the single biggest eligibility question.
2. **The 20% co-payment trigger age.** Petplan says this is "usually added at the dog's 10th birthday (**7th for some breeds**)". Petplan does not publish the list of which breeds trigger at 7, and it doesn't state how a mixed breed is classified. On a 2-year-old this is 5–8 years away, but over a lifetime policy it materially changes long-term cost.

Petplan also states the **fixed excess varies by "the type of dog you have"** — so the excess itself is breed-influenced.

## What depends on an individual quote

- **The actual excess amount at either insurer.** Petplan explicitly says get a quote; Waggel's is adjustable by the customer. Neither can be assumed.
- **Premiums**, which are the real deciding factor and depend on breed, postcode and chosen limit.
- **Waggel's underwriting acceptance.** I found no breed exclusion and no Dangerous Dogs Act clause anywhere in Waggel's Standard Policy Wording (V21) — "breed" appears only in the pet-details and pedigree-documentation sections. That is an absence of evidence, not a confirmed absence of a rule: acceptance criteria can still be applied at quote stage.

## What the owner must verify before buying

1. Whether the dog could be considered a **banned type** under the DDA — decisive for Petplan eligibility.
2. Ask Petplan directly **whether their dog's breed mix triggers the 20% co-payment at 7 or 10**, and get it in writing.
3. The **exact fixed excess** on each quote, at the same cover level, for a like-for-like comparison.
4. Whether the dog has **any dental history already on file** — a pre-existing dental note would be excluded by Waggel and would likely also be excluded by Petplan.
5. That they can realistically commit to the **annual dental exam** at either insurer, since both make dental cover conditional on it.

## Conditional recommendation

**Choose Petplan Covered For Life if** unlimited-within-the-annual-limit dental cover is the priority. Dental illness in dogs escalates into multi-tooth extractions and periodontal surgery that can run well past £1,000, and Petplan is the only one of the two where a large dental bill isn't capped separately. This holds *provided* the dog is not DDA-type and *provided* the 7-year co-payment trigger doesn't apply to its breed mix.

**Choose Waggel if** the priority is a **high overall annual limit** (£15k), **control over excess and co-payment**, and **avoiding a forced 20% co-payment in later life** — which is exactly when a lifetime policy earns its value. The £1,000 dental cap is the price you pay for that.

**On the stated criteria specifically** — cover levels, vet-fee limits, dental treatment, and excess/co-payment structure — the deciding trade-off is narrow: **Petplan wins on dental depth and claim-deadline flexibility; Waggel wins on headline limit, excess flexibility, and long-run co-payment cost.** If the dental exam requirement is comfortably met and no DDA concern exists, Petplan's uncapped dental is the stronger fit for the requested criteria. If there is *any* doubt about the breed mix, Waggel is the lower-risk starting point, because its confirmed £1,000 dental cap is a known, quantified limitation — whereas Petplan's breed exposure is currently unquantified.

One caveat on method: some search-result summaries surfaced these figures first, but I did not rely on them — every number and clause above was confirmed on Petplan's own product/FAQ pages and in Waggel's Standard Policy Wording V21 and FAQ pages.
